title: Landing in Tokyo with No Plan (First 24 Hours)
creator: Theo Walks the World
description:
First day in Tokyo: Narita to Asakusa on the train, a tiny ramen counter, getting lost in Ueno and a 7-Eleven haul at midnight.

Gear: Sony ZV-E10, Rode Wireless Go
Music: Epidemic Sound

Instagram: @theowalkstheworld

sentences.t: Okay, we have landed in Tokyo, it is six in the morning, and I have slept maybe two hours on that flight.
I have no hotel check-in until three, no real plan, and I am so excited.
First problem, I need to get from Narita into the city, and I need maps to do that.
So before I even get to passport control, I'm setting up data on my phone.
I bought an Airalo eSIM for Japan before I left, so I'm just going into settings, mobile data, and switching the line on.
Data roaming on for the eSIM, off for my home SIM, so I don't get some horrible bill.
And there we go, four bars, 5G, and I'm still standing at the gate.
Let me open maps, and okay, it's saying the Keisei line to Asakusa, about an hour and ten minutes.
I'm also topping up my train card in the app right now, which you can't do without data, by the way.
And I can check in the Airalo app that I've used about forty megabytes of my ten gigs, so I'm fine for the whole week.
Okay, quick thing while I'm walking to the train, Airalo is actually sponsoring today's video.
If you travel a lot, it's the easiest way I've found to get data abroad, you install it before you fly and you're online the second you land.
They have eSIMs for over two hundred countries, and it's usually way cheaper than your carrier's roaming plan.
Use code THEOWALKS for fifteen percent off your first eSIM, and the link is in the description.
Alright, here's the train.
I love how quiet Japanese trains are, nobody is on the phone, everybody is just reading or asleep.
I'm going to try very hard not to fall asleep and miss my stop.
Okay, we're in Asakusa, and it is still only eight thirty.
This is Kaminarimon, the big red gate with the giant lantern, and because it's so early, there's hardly anyone here.
I've seen photos of this street totally packed, so this feels like a secret.
The shops on Nakamise are only just opening up, and this lady is already making these little sweet bean cakes.
I'm getting one, obviously.
Oh, it's still warm, that is so good, it's like a soft little pancake with sweet red bean inside.
Okay, I need actual food, and someone told me there's a tiny ramen place near here that opens at ten.
It's ten-oh-two and there is already a line, which is always a good sign.
You order from a vending machine at the door, you put your money in, press the button, and hand the ticket to the chef.
There are eight seats, that's it, eight seats at the counter.
I went with the shoyu ramen, and look at this, the broth is so clear you can see the noodles right through it.
That is unbelievable, and it was about nine dollars.
Okay, it's the afternoon now, I'm in Ueno park, and I'm officially hitting the wall.
Jet lag is real, my legs feel like they're made of sand.
But I'm going to push through until check-in, because if I nap now, I'm going to be awake at three a.m.
Update, I did not push through, I fell asleep on a bench for twenty minutes.
Totally worth it.
Tomorrow I'm heading to Shibuya and trying to find this record shop a friend told me about, so stick around for that one.
See you tomorrow, Tokyo.
